summary: Hostname sanitization truncation causing Azure AD join failures for staged image devices
description:
Issue summary:
During the staged imaging wave (wave-12) several laptops fail to complete Azure AD (AAD) join during Autopilot enrollment. The devices report a name collision or registration error and drop back into the OOBE loop.

Impact:
- ~18 devices in this wave failed to enroll (blocking prep for new hires).
- Devices remain stuck in OOBE, requiring manual intervention from IT.
- Delays for desk assignment and provisioning; potential inventory/accounting mismatches in assetdb.

Environment:
- Staged image build: internal-imaging-2026.02.28
- Provisioning pipeline: corp-autopilot-prod/us-east
- Affected regions: us-east (primary), one repro in eu-west in staging lab

Steps to reproduce:
1) Image a Dell Latitude 7440 with the staged image and default naming template (asset tag + plant code).
2) Run the imaging script which sanitizes hostnames (removes non-alphanumeric characters and enforces max length).
3) Reboot to Autopilot; observe Autopilot attempt to join device to AAD.
4) Autopilot reports failure and device returns to OOBE.

Observed logs / error messages:
- Autopilot UI: "Device registration failed: duplicate device name"
- MDM logs: "AADJoinError: RegistrationFailure (DeviceNameCollision)"
- Imaging logs: "hostname_sanitize() -> asset-PLANT-123456 -> assetPLANT123456 -> truncated to assetPLANT123"

Notes: Hostnames are being truncated to 12 characters after sanitization. When two asset tags only differ beyond the 12-char prefix, collisions occur and AAD rejects registration. The truncation appears to be an older compatibility value left in the sanitization routine (historically for legacy on-prem DNS constraints).
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by support: confirmed 18 failed enrollments in wave-12 and one lab repro. SRE captured imaging logs and Azure registration traces for three devices. Hypothesis: sanitization function strips separators and then enforces a legacy 12-char limit which produces non-unique names for devices whose uniqueness relies on trailing characters.

Evidence:
- Imaging script commit history shows a hard-coded TRUNCATE_LEN=12 introduced 2019-07 for legacy DHCP hostnames.
- AssetDB contains original full asset tag values; device name in the image is the sanitized/truncated value.
- Manual rename in OOBE (to a unique name) allows AAD join to succeed, confirming name collision as root cause.

Temporary mitigation attempted:
- IT manually appended a unique suffix during OOBE for affected devices (workaround) — time-consuming and not scalable.
- Disabled the truncation locally in one lab image and Autopilot join succeeded (proof of fix but not safe to deploy without validation).

2026-03-10 11:05 - Marco Ruiz (Provisioning): Confirmed pattern in logs. All failing hostnames show identical 12-char prefix after sanitization. Repro ready in imaging lab.

2026-03-10 13:40 - Linh Tran (SRE): Pulled Azure MDM traces: 'DeviceNameCollision' returned by Graph API when creating device object. Correlates to sanitized name. Will capture packet traces during Autopilot join for a repro device.
2026-03-11 08:18 - Marco Ruiz (Provisioning): Found commit that introduced TRUNCATE_LEN=12 in legacy script. Suggest bump to 15 and add deterministic hash suffix if asset tag longer than limit.

2026-03-11 14:02 - Eng (Imaging Team) via PR: Requested reproduction steps and a lab device for validation. Created draft PR to change truncation to 15 and append last 3 chars of asset tag as suffix when collision risk detected.
2026-03-12 10:30 - Security (J. Morales): Flagged that names >15 may break legacy on-prem DNS integrations; asked for compatibility validation before changing global behavior.

2026-03-13 16:05 - Marco Ruiz (Provisioning): Running compatibility tests in lab for DNS and DHCP. Preparing a controlled rollout plan and a temporary live workaround for IT (script to detect collisions and prompt unique suffix during OOBE).
workaround: IT temporary process: For devices that fail AAD join, perform manual OOBE 'rename' step and append department code + 3-digit counter (e.g., ASSETPLANT123-ENG001). Script available at: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/blob/main/tools/oobe-rename.sh
next_steps:
1) Eng to land PR that: (a) raises truncation limit to 15, (b) appends deterministic 3-char hash of asset tag when original exceeds limit, and (c) surfaces collisions into imaging logs.
2) SRE to validate DNS/DHCP compatibility with names up to 15 chars in staging and one pilot site.
3) Provisioning to run a 50-device pilot next week using updated script.
4) If pilot passes, schedule global image rebuild and wave re-run; update Confluence and assetdb ingestion pipelines to record both raw asset tag and sanitized hostname.
5) Postmortem and runbook update to avoid recurrence.
